title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger (only the web build does, via `WebLogger`; `main` even had an empty `if RUST_LOG is none {}` block), so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` is discarded, including audio stream errors and plugin failures. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere.

## What

`apps/soundcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (just `log`):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `logs/soundcraft.log` in the settings directory, next to `ui.json`, `Autosave/` and `Presets/` (Linux `~/.config/soundcraft/logs/`). `SOUNDCRAFT_NO_PREFS` runs log to standard error only.
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `soundcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512).
- **Levels:** `info` for `soundcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.

### Realtime safety

A logger that takes a mutex and writes files must never run on the audio thread, and several records can originate there: cpal error callbacks (ALSA repeats `audio stream error` in a loop), `synth.rs` "instrument event queue full", hosted CLAP/VST3/AU `process` errors, CLAP's `host_log`, and the engine panic hook. Because `MixEngine::render` fans strips out to rayon workers (4+ strips), patching each call site would miss records from worker thread…

author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![SoundCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/soundcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the SoundCraft colour field, SoundCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small SoundCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

Same approach as PhotoCraft's and VectorCraft's, which have landed (storytold/photocraft#1201, storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.

title: Fix the crash on quit after a VST3 scan: run module exits on the entry thread
author: ebbicott
body:
Closes #16.

On macOS, any process that had loaded VST3 plugins could segfault on exit when Steinberg's HALion Sonic is installed: the app on quit, `soundcraft-cli`, and the `soundcraft-engine`, `soundcraft-mix` and `soundcraft-vst3-host` unit tests. The VST3 host ran each module's entry but never its exit. The issue has the full diagnosis and crash stacks.

## What changes

All `unsafe` stays in `crates/vst3-host/src/ffi.rs`, each block with a `// SAFETY:` comment.

- **Module exits run, after the factory is released.** For each loaded module, newest first, the host releases the cached factory and then calls the module exit (`bundleExit` / `ExitDll` / `ModuleExit`), as the VST3 SDK's own host does.
- **Up front, before the process exits.** `soundcraft_vst3_host::shutdown()` runs the exits. `soundcraft_engine::shutdown_plugin_hosts()` calls it, and so covers every plugin host in one place.
  - The app calls it from `on_exit`, after releasing its player and with it the plugin instances. `on_exit` runs on every way out, including the system Quit (⌘Q), which calls `exit()` from inside the event loop, so `run_native` never returns.
  - The CLI calls it after its subcommand returns.
- **An exit handler as the fallback.** For any other exit (test binaries, for example), an `atexit` handler runs the exits. It is registered again after each new module, so it runs before the static destructors of every module loaded so far. That is enough after a scan, but too late once a plugin has been used (see testing).
- **On the thread that ran the entry.** Massive X crashes in `bundleExit` on any other thread. Modules asked for on the main thread are entered there, which covers the app and the CLI. Requests from any other thread go to a long-lived `vst3-modules` thread, which also runs their exits, because the requesting thread may be gone by then.
- **Modules still in use are left alone.** That means a module with a live instance, or one whose editor view `EditorLink::kill` had to le…

title: Fix keyboard shortcuts on Windows and Linux: Ctrl is the Cmd key (#15)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #15.

On Windows (and Linux), keyboard shortcuts did not work. No Cmd+ shortcut fired, and Ctrl+S opened Search instead of saving. egui reports a held Ctrl as both `ctrl` and `command` there. The shortcut matcher wanted `ctrl` to be off for a Cmd+ shortcut, and Ctrl+S matched the Cmd+Ctrl+S Search chord.

What changed (crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs):
- Off macOS, a held Ctrl counts as the shortcut's Cmd, so Ctrl+S saves and Ctrl+X cuts. Shortcuts that also need the Mac Control key (Cmd+Ctrl+...) have no key of their own off macOS, so they no longer steal plain Ctrl chords.
- The Cmd+Ctrl+S Search chord works only on macOS. On other platforms, Search is still in the Window menu.

Tests: unit tests in shortcuts.rs check the modifier matching and the Search chord for both macOS and non-macOS. The platform is a parameter, so both cases run on every CI host.

title: Fix input monitoring pitch and dropouts when input and session rates differ
author: Garygunn94
body:
## Problem
Input monitoring fed raw input-device samples to the output callback as if they were at the session rate. When the input device runs at a different rate (e.g. 16 kHz or 44.1 kHz into a 48 kHz session), monitored audio plays too fast (higher pitch) and the buffer runs dry between bursts, so it sounds very quiet.

## Change
- `InputRing` knows the input rate and converts to the session rate with linear interpolation inside `pop_into`. Allocation-free and non-blocking, so the audio thread rules still hold.
- The buffer cap is computed once in `new()`, replacing two formulas that had drifted apart.
- `render_next` passes the session rate into `pop_into`.

## Not in this PR
- Monitoring can start up to 0.5 s behind the input, because the ring keeps filling while monitoring is off.
- There is no jitter cushion, so input bursts can still cause dropouts. Fixing this needs a target fill level, which is a latency decision.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback`: 10/10, including new tests for up-conversion (16 kHz to 48 kHz), down-conversion (96 kHz to 48 kHz), equal rates and underrun.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers and wasm all pass.
- Not tested with real audio hardware.

title: Keep the clip context menu open while moving onto it
author: Garygunn94
body:
## Problem
Right-clicking a recorded clip opened the clip menu, but it vanished as soon as the pointer moved onto it, so Delete could not be reached.

## Cause
The clip menu was attached at the end of `lane_interaction`. That function returns early when the lane has no pointer position. Once the menu is open, the pointer is over the popup, the lane loses its hover, and the menu is never drawn again.

## Change
- Attach the clip menu before the early return.
- Remember the right-clicked clip so the menu keeps its target while in use. The stored id is dropped if the clip no longer exists.
- Add a kittest regression test (`crates/ui-egui/tests/clip_menu.rs`): right-click a clip, move onto the menu, click Delete, and assert the clip is removed. It fails on the previous code.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

title: Default Windows startup to DirectX 12
author: DWAA1660
body:
No SoundCraft issue reports this yet. This is a preventive fix for the same Windows startup crash.

Same fix as storytold/designcraft#168, applied to SoundCraft. FilmCraft has the same change for storytold/filmcraft#179.

## Problem

SoundCraft's desktop app uses eframe's default wgpu instance, which enables `PRIMARY | GL` on Windows. Creating the OpenGL backend can crash inside AMD's OpenGL driver (`atio6axx.dll`) before adapter selection or any Rust error handling runs. The app then flashes in Task Manager and exits with no window and no error (storytold/designcraft#167, storytold/filmcraft#179, storytold/filmcraft#268). `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` was the verified workaround.

## Change

- New `apps/soundcraft/src/graphics.rs`: when no `WGPU_BACKEND` is set, the Windows wgpu instance enables only DirectX 12 before it is created, so OpenGL is never initialized as a fallback. Picking an adapter afterwards would be too late.
- `main.rs` applies it on Windows only. An explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` is still honoured, and the process environment is not changed.
- macOS, Linux and the web build are unchanged.
- README: a short Windows troubleshooting note on the default and the `WGPU_BACKEND` override.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p soundcraft graphics`: 2 passed. `windows_default_initializes_only_dx12` asserts that eframe's default includes GL and that the configured instance is DX12 only. `explicit_backend_override_is_preserved` covers overrides.
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings` (Linux): clean. `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- `cargo check -p soundcraft --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`: clean, so the Windows-only call site compiles.
- Limitation: no Windows/AMD hardware here, so the driver crash itself was not reproduced. The DX12 workaround comes from the designcraft report.

title: Fix debug overflow panic on the first automation-write pass

body:

title: fix(Play Audio): Resume the web AudioContext on the first user gesture
author: hamada147
body:
cpal (wasm) creates its output stream at startup, before any user gesture, so the browser leaves the WebAudio AudioContext 'suspended'. As a result no audio plays, and the transport clock never advances because the audio callback drives it.

Wrap the AudioContext constructor before the wasm module loads so that every context cpal creates is captured. On the first pointer, mouse, touch or key event, resume any context that is still suspended.

Edit 1:
The issue happens on macOS using Google Chrome through web assembly inside of a docker container and connected to SoundCraft on HTTPS using self signed certificate

title: Fix drag selection and the insertion point in the Edit window
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #166: dragging a selection up from the last track deselected it and selected every track above instead. Fixed, along with related Edit-window drag problems:

- Drag selection spans exactly the tracks between the press and the pointer, in either direction, and the whole window updates in the same frame.
- Shift+click in another track adds it to the selection with the same range, as in Pro Tools, so the selected tracks no longer have to be adjacent.
- Track names follow Pro Tools' rules in the Edit window, the Mix window and the Tracks list: Shift+click selects every track between the nearest selected one and the clicked one, and Cmd+click (Ctrl+click on Windows and Linux) adds or removes one. A click on a name used to replace the selection.
- Dropping a track's name plate lower down no longer sends the track to the end.
- Drags act where you pressed: a quick drag from a clip edge now trims instead of moving the clip.
- Dragging past the edge of the track area scrolls, and a flick past the last track selects down to it.
- The insertion point moves on press, shows immediately, and only on the selected tracks.
- `edit.select` no longer makes a new document revision when nothing changed (each one is resent to the audio engine).
- Fixes a panic when a fade drag's clip shrinks to zero length.

Tested: 21 new tests (20 UI tests driving real pointer events through `egui_kittest`, one engine test), each failing before its fix. fmt, workspace clippy, `xtask layers`/`assets` and the wasm check pass, and I tried the drags by hand on macOS with the demo session. Not run: the VST3 host tests that abort on machines with third-party VST3s installed.

title: soundcraft-cli --help: stop at the closing code fence, no Rust source lines (#48)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #48

`soundcraft-cli --help` built its text from the module doc comment with `.skip(3).take(14)`, but the usage block is only 11 lines long. So the output ended with the closing code fence, `#![deny(...)]`, a blank line and `use serde_json::{Value, json};`.

This adds a small `help_text()` that takes doc lines until the closing fence (`take_while(|l| l.trim_end() != "//! ```")`) instead of a fixed count. `--help` now uses it. The help still follows the doc comment if commands are added or removed later.

Test: `help_text_is_only_the_usage_block` checks that the help starts with the `info` line, ends with the `plugins` line, and has no code fence and no Rust source. It fails with the old `take(14)` slice.

Only the help output changes.

title: CLI: run --cmd and app reject malformed JSON instead of using empty params (#50)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #50

`soundcraft-cli run --cmd ID=JSON` parsed the params with `serde_json::from_str(p).unwrap_or(json!({}))`. With malformed JSON (for example a missing closing brace) the command ran with default params and exited 0, or failed later with a misleading missing-parameter error. `app METHOD [JSON]` did the same with `.ok().unwrap_or(json!({}))`.

This adds a small `parse_cmd_spec()` for the `--cmd` argument. `ID` alone still gives `{}`. `ID=JSON` with invalid JSON now returns `ID: bad JSON: <serde error>`, and `run` exits 1 before it executes that command. `app` now fails the same way when its JSON argument is given but does not parse; an omitted argument still gives `{}`. The message matches the one `script` already prints.

Tests: `cmd_spec_parses_id_and_json` checks a bare id and a valid `ID=JSON`. `cmd_spec_rejects_truncated_json` checks that `a.b={"x":` is an error; with the old `unwrap_or` it would have given `{}`.

Only the parsing of these JSON arguments changes. Valid and omitted params work as before.

title: convert and bounce: refuse output extensions the encoder cannot write instead of saving WAV data (#47)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #47.

`soundcraft-cli convert in.wav out.mp3` and `run --bounce mix.mp3` (and `.ogg`, `.m4a`, `.xyz`, ...) used to fall through to the WAV encoder, write PCM WAV under that name and exit 0.

- `soundcraft-audio-io` gets `encode_format_for(name)`, which maps an extension or format name (case-insensitive, leading dot allowed) to the `FileFormat` that `encode` really writes (`wav`, `aif`/`aiff`, `flac`), or `None`. `ENCODE_EXTENSIONS` lists them for error messages.
- `convert` uses it and fails before writing anything: ``out.mp3: cannot write `.mp3` files (supported: wav, aif, aiff, flac)``, non-zero exit code.
- `file.bounce_mix` (which `run --bounce` calls) uses it for both the `format` param and the path extension and returns a bad-params error, so no file is written and the CLI exits non-zero.

A path with no extension still bounces/converts to WAV, as before.

Tests:
- `crates/audio-io/tests/encode_format.rs`: the mapping accepts wav/aif/aiff/flac and rejects mp3/ogg/m4a/xyz.
- `cmd::file::tests::bounce_refuses_formats_it_cannot_write`: bouncing to `.mp3`/`.ogg`/`.xyz` errors and leaves no file; `.flac` still works. Without the fix the `.mp3` bounce succeeds and the test fails.

title: Scan third-party plugins in child processes
author: grovebit
body:
Reading what a VST3 or CLAP file holds runs its code, and SoundCraft did that in-process for every installed plugin, so one bad plugin could take the app down. On a machine with UAD, Waves and NI plugins even `cargo test` aborted, and Kontakt crashed the app on quit.

Now each plugin file is read by a short-lived child (the app run as `--scan-plugin <format> <path>`), a few at a time, with a timeout. A crash or hang costs only that file. It's listed under the CLAP/VST3 insert menus and in `engine.plugin_scan_failures`. Results are cached per user, and only inserted plugins are ever loaded into the app. Scanning stays off until an app calls `soundcraft_engine::plugins::init()`, so tests never load the machine's plugins.

**Policy question:** the children's `_exit` and macOS `LSBackgroundOnly` calls need `unsafe`, so they live in `vst3-host/src/ffi.rs`, and AGENTS.md now says so. Happy to move them into a `plugin-scan` exception instead.

**Tested** on macOS: fmt, clippy, `cargo test --workspace`, `xtask layers`, `xtask assets` and `xtask wasm`. That includes an end-to-end test where a plugin kills its scan child. Not run: Windows, Linux.

title: Show Ctrl instead of Cmd in shortcut text off macOS (#62)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #62.

The command registry stores shortcuts in macOS form ("Cmd+N", "Cmd+Shift+W"), and the UI printed them as stored, so Windows, Linux and the web build showed "Cmd" for keys that are really Ctrl there.

title: Record takes straight to disk
author: grovebit
body:
Takes were kept only in memory until Stop, in a buffer the audio thread kept reallocating, so a crash mid-take lost the whole recording.

- The input callback copies into a preallocated lock-free ring and never locks or allocates; samples that don't fit become silence, and the loss is reported.
- A writer thread streams each armed track's inputs to `<track>_<NN>.wav` in the session's Audio Files (the autosave folder until the session is first saved), rewriting the header every second; if a file can't be created, Record doesn't start and says why.
- At Stop the files become the clips' sources, and Save and autosave use them in place instead of copying them.
- Loop recording keeps one file per track, with one clip per pass on its own playlist, in one undo step.

Tested: 507 workspace tests pass (6 tests that load this Mac's installed VST3 plugins skipped), plus fmt, clippy -D warnings, layers, assets and wasm. Recorded live takes on macOS; a SIGKILL mid-take leaves a playable file.

title: Add a built-in Sampler instrument

body:
Adds a sampler as a third built-in instrument next to the synth and drum synth. Roadmap focus #3, plugin depth.

What it does:
- plays one sample across the keyboard, 32 voices, cubic interpolation
- root note, transpose, fine tune, key tracking on or off
- key range and velocity range
- ADSR with velocity sensitivity
- sample start, forward or ping-pong loop

title: Stop playback when replacing the session
author: reoniazx
body:
Creating a new session while playback is running leaves the old audio player or simulated clock running, so the playhead continues moving in the new project.

Reset transport status and discard pending transport requests whenever the session document is replaced. The UI stops and resets the old playback/capture state before sending the new session to the audio thread, without applying stop-time insertion or scrolling edits to the replacement document. This also covers opening, closing and reverting a session through the shared replacement path.

Validation:
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch independently of the other fixes.
- Regression tests cover ongoing playback, a Play request queued before the next frame, replaying the new session, preserving the replacement session's selection and clean state, and an invalid New Session request leaving the existing transport unchanged.
- Playback regressions use the simulated clock; they do not open an audio device.

title: Keep the playhead visible while playback is stopped
author: reoniazx
body:
The red playhead disappears when playback stops; the remaining insertion cursor blinks and requires a track selection.

Draw a persistent playhead across the Edit window's rulers and track area, and in the Universe overview. It follows the transport while playing and marks the edit insertion while stopped, including an empty session or a range selection. Playback auto-scrolling keeps its existing behavior.

Validation:

- A rendering regression checks the full-height line with no tracks, point and range selections, stopped and playing transport states, and different frame times.
- Offscreen screenshots were inspected in Dark and Light themes and with an empty session.

title: Support anchored trackpad zoom and smooth timeline navigation
author: reoniazx
body:
Pinch events do not zoom the Edit timeline, scrolling over rulers is ignored, and Shift+scroll is remapped a second time after egui has already converted it to horizontal movement.

Handle continuous pinch and Cmd/Ctrl+scroll zoom around the pointer through a new shared `view.zoom_at` command. Consume two-axis scrolling in the hovered Edit viewport, including rulers and track headers, preserve small deltas and native momentum input, and pause playhead following when manually panning away during playback. Timeline scrolling now uses saturating arithmetic at extreme offsets.

Add validated `ui.scroll` and `ui.zoom` control-channel methods for exercising the same pointer-input path, and document the gesture mappings and command parameters.

Validation:
- `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch independently of the other fixes.
- Six UI regressions cover anchored ruler pinch, two-axis scrolling and movement after finger release, Shift scrolling, continuous Cmd scrolling, isolation from other panels, and manual panning during playback.
- Engine tests cover anchor preservation, invalid zoom parameters and numeric limits; control-channel tests reject malformed gestures without queuing partial input.
- Before/after zoom and pan screenshots were inspected. Gesture tests use synthetic events; physical trackpad testing has not been performed.

title: Keep the MIDI editor dock at its resized height
author: reoniazx
body:
Dragging the MIDI Editor’s top edge could not retain the chosen height: its painter-only contents never claimed the resized space, so egui collapsed the dock to its 260-point minimum on subsequent frames.

Call `ui.take_available_space()` before painting, including the empty state. The dock now starts at its configured 320-point height, resizes in both directions, and preserves its chosen height when closed and reopened during the same app session.

Regression tests exercise the real editor with and without a selected MIDI clip. They cover enlargement, shrinking, the existing minimum height, persistence after release and reopening, timeline separation, and unchanged session data.

title: Linux: default to XWayland for file drag-and-drop on Wayland desktops
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Rationale & History

Under Wayland sessions, dragging and dropping audio files, MIDI files, or session projects from desktop file managers onto SoundCraft showed a "no" (prohibited) cursor and drops did not arrive.

This occurs because `eframe 0.36.2` depends on `winit 0.30.13`. In `winit 0.30`, Wayland drag-and-drop was not implemented ([winit#1881](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/1881)). Native Wayland drag-and-drop was added for `winit 0.31` in [winit#4571](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4571) (merged July 2026, tagged in `0.31.0-beta.3`). However, updating to `winit 0.31` directly is blocked by breaking event loop API changes until upstream `eframe` adds support.

On X11 / XWayland, drag-and-drop is fully supported in `winit 0.30`. This pull request adopts the established pattern from `designcraft` and `deckcraft` by Brandon Thomas:
1. Adds `winit = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = ["x11"] }` under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
2. Adds an event loop builder hook before running the native event loop: when an X server is reachable (`DISPLAY` is set) and `SOUNDCRAFT_WAYLAND` is not set, configures `EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11()` to route through XWayland so file drops work out of the box on standard Wayland desktop sessions.
3. Allows users desiring pure native Wayland to opt out and preserve the native Wayland backend by setting `SOUNDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`.

### Verification
Verified local compilation and dependency resolution with `cargo check -p soundcraft` on Linux (0 errors, 0 warnings).

title: Play built-in instruments with their saved parameters (#152)
author: joshuamontierth
body:
Fixes #152.

## Cause

The mixer never pushed a built-in instrument's session parameters into the plugin. Inserts get `apply_params` before every block. The instrument branch of the strip render went straight to `schedule_notes` + `process`, so the instance kept its factory defaults. Every saved built-in instrument parameter was ignored, not only `level` (cutoff, envelopes, drum tuning...). This affected bounces and realtime playback alike, since both use `MixEngine`.

## Fix (`crates/mix/src/lib.rs`)

- **Per block:** the instrument branch calls `apply_params` for built-in instruments, the same way inserts do. Only changed values are pushed, so session edits still reach a live instance.
- **At creation:** `SlotCtx::make` sets a new built-in instance's session parameters and resets it. Without this, smoothed parameters (the instruments' `level`) start at the default and glide to the saved value over the first ~20 ms. The new test fails at sample 1 without this step. This also applies to built-in inserts. A Gain insert at −12 dB now starts the bounce at −12 dB instead of fading down from 0 dB.
- **Automation:** `apply_params` found plugin automation lanes with `u8::try_from(i).unwrap_or(0)`, so `INSTRUMENT_SLOT` (`usize::MAX`) would have read insert **a**'s lanes. It now matches insert slots only. Inserts behave exactly as before (their index always fits in `u8`).
- **Hosted (CLAP/VST3/AU) instruments are unchanged.** Their sound comes from the restored state and their own editor, and `instrument.params` isn't kept in step with them (the plugin window says so). Pushing those values would overwrite a loaded patch.

title: fix(mix): push an instrument's stored params to its plugin before each block (#152)
author: rollroyces

## Summary

The app is signed before that, so SoundCraft.app inside the released DMG, and any `ditto` copy of it, fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict` with "resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed". The script only re-checked the DMG's own signature after imaging, so this went unnoticed.

This is the fix PdfCraft and LightCraft already shipped (https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/823, https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/959), ported to `packaging/macos/package.sh`:

- The image is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder … -fs HFS+ -format UDZO` instead of `makehybrid` + `convert`. `create` attaches a device while it copies and can hit "Resource busy" on CI runners, so it gets up to five tries with growing pauses.
- `xattr -cr` on the bundle before signing, so nothing picked up during the build ends up under the signature.
- After the DMG is signed, the script mounts it read-only and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the app inside and on a `ditto` copy of it, plus `spctl --assess` on the copy when notarizing. Any failure stops the release and prints the app's xattrs.
- The volume name stays `SoundCraft` and `.DS_Store` / `.background` are copied as before, so the window layout is unchanged.
- `packaging/macos/dmg/README.md` no longer says the DMG is built with `makehybrid`.

Testing: I don't have a Mac, so this was not run. I checked the script with `bash -n` and shellcheck 0.11 (clean) and compared it line by line with the PdfCraft change, which was verified on macOS (the new gate passes, and fails with the old `makehybrid` lines put back). The release workflow's macOS job is what will actually exercise it; the new check after imaging makes that job fail loudly if something is off.

title: Windows: compile DX12 shaders with FXC
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
On Windows the app quit right after the window appeared with "Parent device is lost". wgpu's default DX12 shader compiler (`Auto`) loads whichever `dxcompiler.dll` it finds on the DLL search path. SoundCraft ships none, and without a matching `dxil.dll` DXC warns that the DXIL is unsigned. wgpu treats that warning as a compile error, its indirect-validation pipeline fails and the device is lost.

The fix sets the DX12 compiler to FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows) in `graphics::configure`, next to the existing DX12-only backend default. `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` still overrides it for troubleshooting, the same way `WGPU_BACKEND` overrides the backends. This is the same change as storytold/cadcraft#613 (and storytold/lightcraft#484, storytold/gridcraft#382). The README's Windows troubleshooting section mentions it.

Tested with a unit test in graphics.rs that starts from `Auto` and checks `configure` leaves FXC. It failed before the change and passes now, and a second test checks an explicit compiler choice is kept. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (all 6 steps).

Not verified: I built on Linux only, where the `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` call in main.rs isn't compiled (no Windows target installed here), so Windows CI is what checks that line. Nobody ran it on a Windows machine.

title: Consolidate covers the whole edit selection (#164)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Consolidate clamped its range with `bounded_to_track`, which stops one second after the last clip on the track. On an empty track a 0-5 s selection gave a 1 s clip, and a 2-7 s selection gave no clip at all while the command still reported success.

`io::consolidate` no longer uses that bound. It turns the selection into a start and length in samples once and uses the same range for the render, the clear and the new clip, so it never clears more than it places. Empty tracks get a silent clip the length of the selection. If the selection is longer than the render cap (`MAX_RENDER_SAMPLES` divided by the track's channel count, about 93 minutes for stereo at 48 kHz), the command returns an error and leaves the session as it was, instead of placing a shorter clip.

Prepare DPE tracks also calls this function. It now applies `bounded_to_track` itself, so each track still consolidates to its own material plus a second, as before. Strip Silence, transient detection and audio-to-MIDI keep the bound too.

Tests in `crates/engine/tests/consolidate_selection.rs`:
- empty tracks with a 0-5 s and a 2-7 s selection get one clip each covering the selection
- a 1 s clip with a 0-5 s selection becomes one 5 s clip that keeps the audio
- multi-track consolidate with a clip on one track is one undo step, and undo restores every track
- a selection over the render cap is refused and nothing changes
- Prepare DPE with existing clips gives the same lengths as before

Five of these fail when the old clamp is put back. The Prepare DPE one passes either way, since it checks that the old behaviour stays.

I ran fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, the tests for soundcraft-engine, the wasm check for soundcraft-engine and `xtask layers`. I left the full workspace run to CI. I haven't tried it by hand in the app.

Fixes #164

title: control server: bound request lines and concurrent connections
author: SteamSmith
body:
## Summary

`apps/soundcraft/src/control_server.rs` (the opt-in `--control` loopback channel) read request lines with `BufRead::lines`, which buffers an entire line before anything checks its size, and spawned one thread per accepted connection with no limit.

- **Bounded line reads:** each line is read with `take(MAX_LINE + 1).read_until(b'\n', …)`. A line longer than `MAX_LINE` = 256 MiB (generous, since requests can carry documents or media as base64) gets an error reply and the connection is closed, without buffering the rest. Previously there was no line limit at all.
- **Connection cap:** at most `MAX_CONNECTIONS` = 16 connections are served at once; further ones get `{"ok": false, "error": "too many control connections"}` and are closed. A slot is released when its connection ends, including if its thread can't start or panics (`Drop` guard).

- `requests_are_answered_with_their_ids`: end to end over a loopback socket with a stand-in UI

author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #241.

With a sample rate like `1e30`, the shortest lag in `yin` saturates to `usize::MAX` and `min_tau + 2` overflows. `audio_to_notes` goes through `yin`, so both panicked. The check is now `min_tau.saturating_add(2)`, so an impossible lag range ends in the `None` ("no pitch") the function already returns for frames it can't analyse.

Validation:
- two unit tests next to `silence_and_garbage` (`yin` at 1e30 and `f32::MAX`, `audio_to_notes` at 1e30) panic with "attempt to add with overflow" on main and pass here
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-dsp` passes
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-dsp --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(track): vca: null clears a VCA assignment, as documented (#237)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #237.

`track.vca` documents `vca: null` as "no VCA", but it passed the value to `track_param`, which rejects `null` ("must be a track id or name"). Only an absent key cleared the assignment. `track.vca` now treats an explicit `null` as absent, the same way `plugin_state` does. `track_param` is unchanged, because the other commands that use it keep rejecting `null`.

Validation:
- new test `cmd::track::tests::vca_null_clears_the_assignment`:
  - `null` clears the assignment, and undo restores it;
  - `true`, an unknown id, an unknown name and a non-VCA track are still errors and leave the assignment alone.
  - It fails on main with `BadParams("track.vca", "`vca` must be a track id or name")`.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine` passes, `hostile_params` included.
- clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(control): apply the engine.commands filter to UI commands (#255)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #255.

`engine.commands {filter}` filtered the engine's rows, but the control handler then appended all 64 `UI_COMMANDS` rows unfiltered. So `filter: "zzzznomatch"` still returned every `window.*` / `ui.*` command. The UI rows now go through the same predicate as the engine (id or label substring, ASCII case-insensitive). The engine's predicate is a closure inside `cmd!`, so it's mirrored in `control.rs` with a comment pointing back to it. An absent or empty filter still lists everything.

Validation:
- `tests/commands_filter.rs` (the file the issue proposes): a filter matching one UI id, a label-only match, mixed case, and no match. It fails on main with all 64 UI rows. Dropping the label match or the lowercasing each fail a case.
- `absent_or_empty_filter_lists_every_ui_command` guards the other direction.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(window): keep the MIDI Editor open on Bring to Front (#254)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #254.

`window.midi_editor` and `window.midi_front` shared one arm that toggled `show_midi_editor`. So Window › MIDI Editor › Bring to Front closed an editor that was already open. `window.midi_front` now shows it and returns `{"value": true}`, like `window.workspace_front`. `window.midi_editor` still toggles.

Validation:
- `tests/midi_front_visibility.rs` (the file the issue proposes) goes through the real menu path (`command_for_path` + `invoke_menu`). Bring to Front twice keeps the editor open, and Bring to Front shows a closed editor. It fails on main with "Bring to Front hid the editor".
- `the_midi_editor_command_still_toggles` catches the opposite mistake.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

The `window.close | window.hide_floating` arm that #216 touches is left alone.

title: fix(midi-editor): a selected video clip is not a MIDI target (#258)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #258.

The MIDI editors find their clip with `!c.is_audio()`, which a video clip also passes. Selecting a video clip made it the "MIDI" target, so the editor went empty, and the Event List and MIDI Keyboard pointed at it too. The check is now `matches!(c.content, ClipContent::Midi { .. })`. All three callers (`score_editor.rs`, and the Event List and MIDI Keyboard in `windows.rs`) only ever want a MIDI clip.

Validation:
- `a_selected_video_clip_is_not_a_midi_target` in `tests/midi_panel.rs` covers two selections. A lone video clip gives no target; on main it gives `Some(ClipId(..))`. With `[video, midi]` selected, the MIDI clip is the target, which rules out a fix that just stops at the first non-MIDI clip.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(video-universe): filmstrip thumbnails use the clip's own movie time (#225)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #225.

In the Video Universe filmstrip, `(x - r.min.x) / r.width() * end` is already the timeline position, but the code added `c.start` again (minus `c.start.min(0)`). So for a clip after zero every thumbnail came from `2 × start` into the movie. For clips at or before zero that extra term cancelled out, which is why it only showed up for later clips.

The computation moved into a small pure `strip_position()` that leaves the clip start out of the sum. Results for clips at or before zero are unchanged.

Validation:
- `strip_position_is_the_timeline_position_for_clips_after_zero` fails with the old formula (`96000` vs `48000`) and passes here.
- `strip_position_is_unchanged_for_clips_at_or_before_zero` pins the old behaviour, including the clamp to the clip start.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(window): Hide All Floating Windows also hides Automation (#253)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #253.

Window › Hide All Floating Windows cleared Transport, Big Counter, Memory Locations, Undo History, Session Info and Audio Health, but not Automation. One line adds `show_automation = false` to the same arm. I checked with `git merge-tree` that it merges cleanly with #216, which splits that arm.

Validation:
- `tests/hide_floating.rs` (the issue's test) fails on main with "Automation must be hidden" and passes here.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

Other floating windows (Color Palette, Disk Usage, Task Manager, Metadata…) also stay open. The issue only asks about Automation, so I left them; happy to add them if you want Hide All to cover every one.

title: fix(edit-window): Pencil clicks on plugin lanes use the plugin's range (#224)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #224.

A Pencil click on a plugin automation lane took its value range from `param.range()`, which for plugin parameters is the generic `(f32::MIN, f32::MAX)`. So the click produced no usable value ("bad parameters for automation.set_point: value required") and no point was added. Dragging already uses `plugin_range(track, &param)`; the click now does too.

Validation:
- `a_pencil_click_on_a_plugin_lane_uses_the_plugin_range` (kittest, demo session, Kick's `plugin:a:input_gain` lane) clicks a quarter of the way down the lane and expects one point at −12 dB. On main it adds no point and shows the issue's error.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

The range lookup now appears in three places (draw, drag, click). I didn't pull it into a helper, to keep this small next to #209 and #216.

title: fix(midi-editor): Quantize snaps to the grid the editor shows (#226)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #226.

The MIDI editor's Quantize button always sent `"grid": "1/16"`, whatever grid the editor showed. `grid_ticks` was only computed after the toolbar was drawn. It's now computed first and passed as a number, which `event.rs`'s `grid_ticks` accepts (clamped to 1..15360 ticks).

Validation:
- `tests/midi_quantize.rs` clicks the real "Quantize" button. `quantize_follows_a_quarter_note_grid` gets 240 instead of 0 on main and passes here. `quantize_follows_a_sixteenth_note_grid` also passes on main: it only shows the click lands and 1/16 is unchanged.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

This moves a block that #137 also edits nearby, so one of the two will need a small rebase.

title: fix(eq): switches and choices redesign the filter on a running EQ (#239)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #239.

On a running EQ, `update()` snapped switch and choice parameters (HPF/LPF on, filter types…) into the smoothers. But `process` only redesigned the filters while a continuous smoother was still settling, so a switch flipped mid-playback didn't take effect. `update()` now calls `redesign()` when a snapped value changes. It doesn't allocate, so it's fine on the audio thread.

Validation:
- `eq_switches_and_choices_apply_to_a_running_eq` in `tests/plugins.rs` covers the issue's 7 cases, Channel Strip included. Each compares the instance changed while running with one built fresh with the new setting, within 0.1 dB. A guard checks that the two settings differ by more than 3 dB, so the comparison means something. On main all 7 fail with the issue's numbers (e.g. `eq_7band hpf_on=1: live -9.03 dB, fresh -33.28 dB`).
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-dsp` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(video): H.264 parameter sets check their arithmetic before range checks (#251, #252)
author: marcoarnulfo

title: fix(markers): markers.edit applies the documented name (#236)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #236.

`markers.edit` documents `name` as the new name, but `edit_marker` only read `rename` (the key the Memory Locations panel sends), so `{"id": 1, "name": "Chorus"}` returned `{}` and changed nothing. It now takes `rename` first and falls back to `name`. When `name` is the selector (no `id` or `number`), the location already has that name, so nothing changes there. `color` is also documented and still ignored; I left it out of this PR.

Validation:
- `edit_marker_renames_with_documented_name` in `cmd/event.rs` renames one location by `id` and the other by `number`, checks the other location keeps its name, and checks that selecting by `name` still works. On main it fails with `("Verse", "Outro")` instead of `("Chorus", "Outro")`.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::event` and `--test hostile_params` pass, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(clip): Elastic Properties stretches the clip by the requested ratio (#227)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #227.

`elastic` set `stretch = ratio` on the clip it passed to `render_stretched`. That helper reads `length / stretch` source samples and stretches them to `out_len = length * ratio`, so the ratio was applied twice. At ratio 2 it rendered only the first half of the clip, stretched 4x, which is how a clip that is silent then tone came out all silent. At 0.5 it read past the clip's end, and at 4 and 0.2 it asked for 16 and 0.04 and was rejected. The clip handed to the renderer is now the unwarped base clip as it plays, the same way `edit.tce_to_timeline` and `clip.remove_pitch_shift` call the helper. `render_stretched` and its other callers are unchanged.

Validation:
- New `elastic_properties_stretches_the_clip_material` in `cmd/clip.rs` uses a synthetic mono source. At ratio 2, a clip that is silent then tone keeps the tone. At ratio 0.5, a silent clip on a longer source stays silent. Ratios 4 and 0.2 give 80,000 and 4,000 samples. On main each of the three parts fails separately: "the tone in the second half was lost", "audio from past the clip end leaked in", and `stretch ratio 16.000 is outside 0.1..10`.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib` for `cmd::clip`, `cmd::clip_more` and `tce_fits_timeline` passes, including the existing `elastic_warp_renders_and_remove_warp_restores`. Clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(dsp): pitch_shift reaches ±48 semitones (#243)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #243.

`pitch_shift` accepts ±48 semitones but hands the whole factor to `time_stretch`, which clamps to 0.1..=10. Anything past about +39.9 or -39.9 semitones came out as a 10x (or 0.1x) shift, so +48 gave 4400 Hz from a 440 Hz tone instead of 7040. When the factor is outside that range, it is now split into two `time_stretch` passes by its square root (4 and 4 for +48, 0.25 and 0.25 for -48). Factors inside the range still take the single pass, so ±24 and everything AudioSuite sends is unchanged.

Validation:
- New `pitch_shift_reaches_the_ends_of_its_range` in `tests/offline_meters.rs` shifts a 440 Hz sine by +40, +48, -40 and -48 and checks the frequency within 0.2%. On main, +40 measures 4400.0 Hz instead of 4434.9. If only the upward case is split, -40 measures 44.0 Hz instead of 43.65. With the fix, +48 measures 7040.0 Hz and -48 measures 27.48 Hz.
- The existing +12 and -7 checks (`pitch_shift_preserves_length_and_shifts`) and the rest of `offline_meters` pass, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(dsp): chorus and flanger tails follow their feedback (#242)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #242.

`ModFx::tail_samples` reported a fixed 200 ms for chorus and flanger, whatever the feedback. With chorus at 30 ms / 90% the echoes stay above -60 dB for about two seconds, so `apply_plugin_with_tail` cut them off. The tail now works like the delay plugin's: the number of repeats for the feedback to fall by 60 dB, times the longest delay in the sweep (base delay plus up to 6 ms of depth for chorus, base delay for flanger). It uses the absolute feedback because the flanger allows negative values, and it never goes below the old 200 ms. It's plain arithmetic on the parameters, with no allocation.

Validation:
- New `modulation_tail_covers_feedback_echoes` in `tests/plugins.rs` sends an impulse through chorus (30 ms, 90%) and flanger (10 ms, +95% and -95%), renders 5 s, and checks that the last sample above -60 dB falls inside `tail_samples()`. On main it fails with `chorus feedback 90: echo at 95039, tail 9600`. Without the `abs()` the -95% flanger case fails (`echo at 64799, tail 9600`).
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-dsp --test plugins` and `--test offline_meters` pass, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(midi-editor): Backspace in a text field leaves the selected notes alone (#223)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #223.

The MIDI editor's Delete/Backspace check read the key from the global input with no focus guard. The editor is drawn before dialogs, so with notes selected, pressing Backspace in the Rename Track field also ran `midi.note_delete`. The check now skips when `egui_wants_keyboard_input()` is true, the same guard the select-all and arrow keys a few lines above already use.

Validation:
- New `tests/midi_editor_keys.rs` selects two notes of the Keys clip with the Rename Track dialog open. It presses Backspace, then Delete, and checks that the name field took the key and the session is unchanged. On main it fails with "Backspace edited the session". A second test checks that both keys still delete the selected notes when no text field has focus.
- `midi_panel`, `rename_dialog` and `shortcuts` still pass, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(edit): cut clip gain keeps the removed gain for paste (#230)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #230.

Cut Special > Clip Gain went through the same `reset_clip_gain` as Clear Special, so it zeroed the selected clips' gain but never filled the clip-gain clipboard: Paste Clip Gain then either had nothing to paste or pasted whatever was copied before. The cut now runs `copy_clip_gain` over the selection first and then resets, so it behaves like Copy followed by Clear in a single undo step. Clear Special is unchanged.

Validation:
- New `cut_clip_gain_can_be_pasted` test: cuts a -6 dB clip with an older -12 dB copy already in the clipboard, checks the source is back at 0 dB and that the paste applies -6 dB. Fails on main (pastes -12 dB), passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib clip_gain` and `--lib cmd::edit`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(track): Clear Trim Automation removes the trim lane (#233)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #233.

`track.clear_trim_automation` was registered with a handler that returned `{}` and did nothing, so the trim written by Trim Automation Write stayed in the session and in the render. It now removes the trim lane (`plugin:255:trim`, the same `trim_param()` that `track.coalesce_trim` drops) from the selected or explicitly named tracks, as one undoable edit, and returns how many tracks it cleared. Volume automation and other tracks are left alone.

Validation:
- New `clear_trim_automation_removes_only_trim` test: clears the selected track, then an explicit one, checks the other track's trim and the volume lane survive and that undo brings the trim back. Fails on main, passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib track`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(edit): Shuffle Clear moves automation with the clips (#232)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #232.

`edit.clear` rippled later clips left in Shuffle mode but never touched automation, so with Automation Follows Edit on the volume points stayed at their old positions while Cut, on the same range, moved them. Clear now does what Cut already does after removing the clips: when Automation Follows Edit is on it clears the lane points inside the range and, in Shuffle, shifts the later points left by the range length. With the option off nothing changes.

Validation:
- New `shuffle_clear_moves_automation_like_cut` test: Shuffle Clear over [4000, 6000) gives volume points at 0, 7000, 18000, the same result as Cut, and leaves them untouched with the option off. Fails on main, passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::edit`, `--test random_edits`, `--test hostile_params`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

One behaviour change to be aware of: with Automation Follows Edit on, Clear in Slip mode now also clears the automation points inside the range, the way Cut already does. The issue's Slip control still passes (its fixture has no point inside the range).

title: fix(event): Constant tempo applies only over its range (#238)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #238.

`event.tempo_constant` shared the handler of `event.tempo`, which reads `at`/`start` and ignores `end`, so it only inserted one tempo change: later changes inside the range stayed active and the new tempo ran on past the end. Constant now works like the other Tempo Operations: it reads the range (explicit `start`/`end`, or the timeline selection), sets the BPM at the start, removes the tempo events strictly inside, and puts back at the end tick the tempo that was in effect there. Both ticks are captured before editing, since the new tempo moves the end in samples. With no range it still inserts a single change, as before.

Validation:
- New `tempo_constant_is_bounded_by_its_range` test: 100 BPM, a 140 BPM change inside [24000, 96000), Constant 90 over that range; checks 100 before, 90 at the start and in the middle, 140 again at the old end tick. Fails on main, passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::event` and `--lib tempo`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(edit): trims stop at the neighbouring clips instead of overlapping them (#228, #229)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #228, fixes #229.

`edit.trim_to_file_boundaries` and `edit.trim_to_fill_selection` extended a clip as far as its source allowed without looking at the other clips on the playlist, so extending across a neighbour left two unfaded clips playing the same region (the constant-source repros in both issues render at double level). Both commands now ask one helper, `trim_limits`, how far the clip may grow: no earlier than the end of the clip before it and no later than the start of the clip after it on the same playlist. I chose to stop at the neighbour rather than overwrite it because that is what the commands that grow an existing clip already do (`edit.paste_merge_midi` and MIDI step input cap the host clip at `next_start`), and because the Edit window's trim handle drag extends through `edit.trim_to_fill_selection`, where eating the next clip would be a surprising result of a drag. A clip with no neighbour still expands to its full source extent as before, and a crossfade the clip already has with a neighbour is kept instead of being trimmed back.

One note on #229: its restoration check expects A to reach its full source length (20,000 frames) by overwriting B. With this change A grows up to B's start (5,000 to 12,000) and B is left intact. If you'd rather have the overwrite semantics of placing a clip, it is a small change in the same helper and I'm happy to switch.

Validation:
- New unit tests in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`: both commands with a neighbour on each side stop at the neighbours with the expected start, end and source offset; a clip with no neighbour expands fully; an existing crossfade overlap survives Trim to File Boundaries. The three neighbour tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::edit`, `--test random_edits`, `--test hostile_params`, `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui --lib edit_window`
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macO…

title: Open .m4b audiobook files like .m4a
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
A user on Discord asked whether SoundCraft can edit their M4B audiobooks without converting them to MP3 first.

M4B is the same MP4/AAC container as M4A, and the decoder already reads it: format detection looks at the `ftyp` box, not the file name, and symphonia's MP4 reader doesn't check the brand. But `.m4b` files never showed up, because the extension was missing from:

- the desktop Open dialog filter (`apps/soundcraft/src/main.rs`)
- the web file picker (`apps/soundcraft-web/src/web.rs`)
- the in-app file browser (`crates/ui-egui/src/windows.rs`)
- the extension fallback in `detect_by_ext` (`crates/audio-io/src/lib.rs`)

This adds `m4b` to all four, plus a test that an `.M4B` hint maps to AAC.

Saving back to M4B is out of scope; export stays WAV/AIFF/FLAC.

title: Apply the Feet+Frames reference to counters and typed positions
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #235.

`setup.current_feet_frames` stored the new origin in `feet_frames.start`, but nothing read it: `format_position` and `parse_position` always counted feet+frames from sample 0. They now take the feet+frames origin next to the timecode start, and two small helpers on `Session` (`format_position`, `parse_position`) pass both, so `session.format_time`, typed positions, the toolbar and big counters, the ruler and the memory locations all use the same reference. The callers that passed `s.timecode_start` by hand now go through those helpers.

Validation: `crates/engine/tests/current_feet_frames_position.rs` sets `12+08` at sample 48000 (30 fps, 48 kHz). On main it reads `1+14` there; here it reads `12+08`, `14+06` at 96000, and typing `feet_frames:14+06` lands back on 96000.

```
cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test current_feet_frames_position
cargo test -p soundcraft-time -- format:: feet_and_frames
cargo clippy -p soundcraft-time -p soundcraft-model -p soundcraft-engine -p soundcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

(macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(mix): pan automation reads the same in playback and bounce
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #244.

Track pan was read once per block, at the block's first sample, and held for the whole block. Bounces render in 1024-frame blocks and playback in callback-sized blocks (up to 512), so the same pan curve landed on different samples: with a -1 -> +1 move over the first 480 samples, the bounce stayed hard left until sample 1023 while playback switched at 512. Now pan automation is read on a fixed 64-sample grid aligned to the timeline, and the routing matrix is applied per grid segment, so any block size gives bit-identical output. Tracks without pan automation keep the single matrix per block. 64 is a trade-off between zipper steps and matrix rebuilds; happy to switch to a smaller step or a per-sample ramp if you prefer.

Volume/trim, send levels and plugin parameters are still sampled per block; I left them alone to keep this to the reported case.

Validation:
- `pan_automation_does_not_depend_on_the_block_size` (soundcraft-mix): fails on main (1024-frame bounce still hard left at sample 600: L 0.5, R 0), passes here; compares 1024 vs 512, 100 and 37-frame renders exactly
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-mix --lib -- pan surround bus send render aux insert`
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-mix --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Create MIDI clips with the Pencil, Consolidate and the MIDI Editor
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #282. An empty MIDI or instrument track had no way to get a clip from the UI, so notes couldn't be entered by hand. `midi.new_clip` existed, but nothing in the UI called it.

- The Pencil draws a MIDI clip on an empty part of a MIDI or instrument track: a click makes one bar, and a drag covers the bars it crosses. Clips start and end on barlines, as Pro Tools does for the MIDI clips it creates, and stop at the next clip instead of overwriting it.
- Consolidate (Option+Shift+3 on macOS, Alt+Shift+3 on Windows and Linux) now works on MIDI and instrument tracks. The selection becomes one clip, gaps included, and an empty selection gives an empty clip. Muted clips stay silent and notes are cut where their clip ended, so it sounds the same.
- With an empty MIDI or instrument track selected, a click in the MIDI Editor adds a clip at the insertion point.
- The new clip is selected, so the MIDI Editor shows it right away.

Tested: CI checks pass locally (685 tests, 7 of them new), apart from six VST3 tests that abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Reorder tracks by dragging them in the Tracks list
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #170. Dragging a track in the Tracks list did nothing. Pro Tools reorders tracks when their names are dragged there, and SoundCraft's Edit window name plates already could.

- Rows can be dragged up and down, and a line shows the gap where the track will land.
- The drop runs `track.move`, so it is one undo step.
- A click still selects the track.

Tested: CI checks pass locally (680 tests, 2 of them new), apart from six VST3 tests that abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Drag or type the tempo in the toolbar
author: grovebit
body:
Part of #189 (its first point). Clicking and dragging the toolbar tempo did nothing. It was painted text, so changing the tempo meant opening Tempo Operations or the tempo ruler.

- The tempo is now a drag value that looks the same until it's hovered. Drag it to change the tempo (hold Shift for steps ten times finer), or click it and type a value from 5 to 1000 BPM.
- It edits the tempo change in effect at the playhead, the one it shows, and leaves later tempo changes alone.
- A whole drag is one undo step.

Tested: CI checks pass locally (681 tests, 3 of them new), apart from six VST3 tests that abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Rename a marker by double-clicking it in the ruler
author: grovebit
body:
Part of #186 ("markers … cannot be renamed"). Double-clicking a marker in a marker ruler added a second marker on top of it, with both labels printed over each other. Renaming was only possible in the Memory Locations list.

- Double-clicking a marker opens a Rename Marker dialog with the old name selected, as Rename Track and Rename Clip do. Pro Tools also opens the memory location when a marker is double-clicked.
- Double-clicking an empty part of the ruler still adds a marker, and a single click on a marker still recalls it.

title: Locate clears plugin and delay-compensation state
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #247.

A locate during playback moved the position and dropped pending output, but never reset the mix engine, so inserts kept their state across the jump: a 5 ms lookahead compressor played 240 frames from the old position and a reverb kept ringing. `Cmd::Locate` now calls `mix.reset()` like Play and Stop already do. On its own that still wasn't enough: `reset()` left the delay-compensation lines (`align`, `align_pre`, `out_extra`) full, and `DelayLine::set` only reallocates when the length changes, so a track aligned behind a latent one still emitted old audio. `reset()` now zeroes them in place (no allocation, no locks on the audio thread).

I put the reset on the transport's Locate rather than in `MixEngine::render`'s "pos != last_end" branch, because that branch also fires on every loop wrap, and flushing there would cut reverb tails and drop the compensated tail at each loop pass. Happy to switch if you'd rather have it in the engine.

Validation:
- `locate_while_playing_drops_the_old_position_audio` (playback, compressor with lookahead and room_reverb): fails on main (compressor audio after the locate), passes here
- `reset_clears_delay_compensation_history` (mix, unprocessed track aligned behind a compressor track): fails on main (old aligned audio after reset), passes here
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-mix -p soundcraft-playback --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Restore Last Selection brings back the previous selection
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #231.

`edit.restore_last_selection` just returned the current range, so nothing was ever remembered to restore. Now `Engine::execute` notes the selection a command replaced (range and tracks) whenever a successful command changes it, so every selection path is covered without touching each command. It lives on the `Engine` next to the clipboard rather than in the document, so selecting still leaves the session clean (`is_dirty`) and it isn't saved with the session; opening another session clears it. Restore swaps it back in, so pressing it twice returns to where you were. With nothing remembered the command is disabled instead of reporting success. I also made it `noundo` like `edit.select`, since a selection change isn't a document edit. Happy to switch either of those.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::edit` / `cmd::edit_more` / `cmd::file` / `cmd::view` / `merge_tests` / `dirty_tests`, `--test session_transport`, `--test random_edits`

title: Apply MIDI track offsets when scheduling notes
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #234.

`event.midi_track_offsets` stored `midi.offset.<track>` in the edit values, but `schedule_notes` in the mix engine never read it, so the notes played where they always had. The scheduler now reads the track's offset once per block and looks that many samples back into the clips, so the track plays exactly as if its MIDI had been moved by the offset (later for positive values, earlier for negative ones). Offline bounce and realtime playback both go through `schedule_notes`, so both pick it up.

Validation: `crates/engine/tests/midi_offset.rs` renders one synth note, sets a 24000-sample offset, resets it to 0, then moves the clip by 24000 instead. On main the offset render is identical to the baseline; here it differs, a zero offset gives the baseline back, and it is sample-identical to the moved-clip render.

```
cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test midi_offset
cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib rtp_and_offsets
cargo clippy -p soundcraft-mix -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

(macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Plugin safety: read plugin state off the audio thread, keep refused settings, contain NaN plugins
author: grovebit
body:
Third-party plugins could hurt a session in three ways: saves read their state on the audio thread, a plugin that refused its saved settings lost them at the next save, and one plugin putting out NaN silenced the whole mix.

- Saves, bounces and autosaves read plugin state on the UI thread, through a handle per CLAP, VST3 and AU instance (like the editor handles). The audio callback no longer calls `save_state`, and a stalled device no longer makes saves wait 2 s.
- A plugin that refuses its stored state keeps it in the session until its own editor is opened, instead of saving its defaults over it.
- The engine checks each insert's and instrument's output. A plugin that puts out NaN or infinity has that block silenced and is skipped until playback stops or starts, and the status line names it.

Tested: 687 tests pass, 9 of them new (state reads from another thread against the CLAP and VST3 fixtures and Apple's AULowpass; NaN from inserts, instruments and the master; refused states). fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass. Six VST3 tests are skipped because they abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Automation passes replace the automation they play over
author: grovebit
body:
A write pass only added points, so the old automation survived between them; a covered window, which runs one pass a second since #192, kept almost all of the old ride.

- `automation.set_point` takes an optional `from`: the points between `from` and `at` are removed first.
- Each point of a pass gives the previous one as `from`, so it replaces everything since then, however far apart the passes run.
- Stop writes a last point where playback stopped.
- A locate or a restart while playing starts afresh, so a jump never erases what it skipped.

Tested: 2 new tests (removing any of the four changes fails the pass test); fmt, clippy, 680 tests pass (6 VST3 tests skipped: they crash on plugins installed on this Mac), assets, layers, wasm.

title: MCP: confine file access with --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root
author: isaac-levine
body:
`soundcraft-cli mcp` gives the agent on the other end the same file access as the user running it. VectorCraft already has two flags for this, so this adds the same ones here with the same names and behaviour, and one client config works across the apps. It is the same change as storytold/wordcraft#798, storytold/gridcraft#480, storytold/deckcraft#247 and storytold/pdfcraft#1448.

    soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

**How it works**

Every file a command reads has to be inside the read root and every file it writes inside the write root. The new `crates/engine/src/file_access.rs` holds the roots and the path logic: make the path absolute, follow symlinks (for a file that doesn't exist yet, resolve its nearest existing ancestor and require the rest to be plain names), then compare with the root by whole path components, so `/work2` is not inside `/work`. On Windows the comparison ignores case and device names like `CON` and `NUL` are refused. Refusals come back as ordinary tool errors with VectorCraft's wording, for example `automation path rejected: outside the read root /work/project: /etc/passwd`.

The checks sit in `crates/engine/src/io.rs`. `session.open`, `file.import_audio`, `file.import_midi`, `file.import_video`, `file.import_clip_groups`, `file.import_session_data`, `track.load_preset` and `mix.sampler_load` used to call `std::fs` themselves. They now go through `io::read_file` and `io::read_text`, and the writers (session save, bounce, stems, clip export, clip groups, `io::replace_file`, the `Audio Files/` and `Backups/` folders next to a saved session) go through `io::write_file`, `io::write_path` and `io::make_dir`. A test walks every file under `crates/engine/src` and fails if one other than `io.rs`, `file_access.rs` and the test files touches `std::fs`, `File::open`, `File::create`, `OpenOptions`, `canonicalize` or the `is_file`, `is_dir` and `exists` probes.
